messages.text: How do changes in Wi-Fi 7/8 technology affect the measurement capability required from Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer?

【推論】Wi‑Fi 7/8 push Signal Generator and Signal Analyzer needs toward wider bandwidth, multi-channel/MIMO operation, and deeper per-link modulation analysis because Wi‑Fi 7 is described with 320 MHz bandwidth, up to 16 spatial streams, 4096QAM and MLO, while Wi‑Fi 8 retains up to 320 MHz, 4096QAM and MLO and adds dRU/UEQM test hurdles [6][13][15].
### Measurement capability impact
| Area | Required capability impact | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Bandwidth | Wi‑Fi 7 requires support for 320 MHz channel bandwidth [6]. | [6] |
| Bandwidth | Wi‑Fi 8 is described as retaining channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz, but this PR summary is not a full normative IEEE 802.11bn specification [15]. | [15] |
| Bandwidth | R&S also demonstrated CMP180 verification of a 480 MHz WLAN waveform as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 candidate, and CMP180 supports bandwidths up to 500 MHz [40]. | [40] |
| Modulation | Wi‑Fi 7 includes 4096QAM, so generator/analyzer capability must cover high-order WLAN modulation [6]. | [6] |
| Modulation | Wi‑Fi 8 is described as retaining 4096QAM from Wi‑Fi 7 [15]. | [15] |
| UEQM | Wi‑Fi 8 UEQM allows each MIMO link to use a different modulation scheme in difficult reception scenarios [1]. | [1] |
| UEQM | UEQM analysis must assess whether the device adapts modulation correctly according to specified MCS combinations [13]. | [13] |
| MIMO | Wi‑Fi 7 is described with up to 16 spatial streams, making multi-stream analyzer/generator capability relevant [6]. | [6] |
| MIMO / MLO | Wi‑Fi 7 MLO makes a test environment with multiple RF chains important [6]. | [6] |
| MIMO / R&S | CMX500 Wi‑Fi 7 R&D tests include MLO, multiple RF chains and 2x2 MIMO [19]. | [19] |
| MIMO / R&S | CMP180 integrates two analyzers, two generators and two sets of eight RF ports to support 2x2 MIMO in one box [19]. | [19] |
| MIMO / R&S | Two CMP180 units can be combined and scaled to four analyzers and generators for 4x4 MIMO access points [19]. | [19] |
| dRU | Wi‑Fi 8 dRU measurements are used to verify uplink transmit power boost and connection reliability improvement [13]. | [13] |
| dRU | dRU is described as a Wi‑Fi 8 feature for overcoming PSD limits [1]. | [1] |
| EVM | WoMT testing includes TX analysis of EIRP, TRP, ACLR and EVM under Wi‑Fi 7 modulation [2]. | [2] |
| EVM | WoMT OTA/RF test confirms EVM, EIRP, TRP, ACLR, EIS, occupied bandwidth and Rx/OOB spurious emissions [27]. | [27] |
| Phase noise | The RAW passages identify R&S FSPN and R&S FSWP as Phase Noise Analyzer and VCO Tester instruments [38][39]. | [38][39] |
| Signaling | R&S and Broadcom will show CMX500 with newly added Wi‑Fi 8 testing capabilities validating a Broadcom prototype Wi‑Fi 8 device [37]. | [37] |
| Signaling | CMX500 is described as supporting WLAN signaling and WLAN TX measurements for 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn and 2x2 MIMO [14]. | [14] |
| Production non-signaling | WLAN production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time, and CMP180 is optimized for this purpose [40]. | [40] |
| Production non-signaling | CMP180 supports Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz with bandwidths up to 500 MHz [40]. | [40] |
| mmWave / IF | For WoMT, native Wi‑Fi/IF/IB band testing uses CMP180, while mmWave signal generation and analysis use CMP200/CMPHEAD50 [2]. | [2] |
| mmWave / IF analyzer | CMP200 IF analyzer bandwidth is up to 1 GHz [28]. | [28] |
| R&D fine tuning | WoMT R&D fine tuning uses FSW67 and signal sources [2]. | [2] |
【推論】For Signal Generator and Signal Analyzer planning, the safest supported floor is 320 MHz and 4096QAM for Wi‑Fi 7/8 core PHY, while a 480 MHz path is only supported as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 waveform candidate demonstrated on CMP180, not as a ratified requirement [15][40].
【推論】For multi-link and MIMO testing, the evidence supports at least 2x2 capability in CMX500/CMP180 contexts and scalable 4x4 with two CMP180 units, but it does not prove coverage of Wi‑Fi 7’s full 16 spatial streams [6][14][19].

- RX analysis：[[EIS]] sensitivity verification。
- Spurious：Rx / OOB spurious emissions monitoring。
- Occupied bandwidth。
- Native Wi-Fi / IF / IB band：[[R&S CMP180]]。
- mmWave signal generation and analysis：[[R&S CMP200]] / [[R&S CMPHEAD50]]。

S-SSS › 基本性質
依 [[S-SSB]]：

- [[S-SSS]] 是 [[Sidelink SSB]] / [[S-SS-PSBCH block]] 的四個組成之一。
- Like standard [[SSS]]，[[S-SSS]] consists of 127 [[BPSK]] modulation symbols。
- Sequence is based on two Fibonacci [[LFSR]]s of length 7：
  - `x0` with taps [7,3]。
  - `x1` with taps [7,6]。
- Final sequence `d` is obtained by interleaving the two LFSR outputs depending on the [[Sidelink identity]]，in same way as standard [[SSS]]；但來源中的完整公式 / identity 符號因轉檔遺失。
- Overall 672 different S-SSS sequences are defined because sequence generation depends on the first and second ID。

| Signaling | CMX500 is described as supporting WLAN signaling and WLAN TX measurements for 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn and 2x2 MIMO [14]. | [14] |
| Production non-signaling | WLAN production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time, and CMP180 is optimized for this purpose [40]. | [40] |
| Production non-signaling | CMP180 supports Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz with bandwidths up to 500 MHz [40]. | [40] |

【推論】For Signal Generator and Signal Analyzer planning, the safest supported floor is 320 MHz and 4096QAM for Wi‑Fi 7/8 core PHY, while a 480 MHz path is only supported as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 waveform candidate demonstrated on CMP180, not as a ratified requirement [15][40].
【推論】For multi-link and MIMO testing, the evidence supports at least 2x2 capability in CMX500/CMP180 contexts and scalable 4x4 with two CMP180 units, but it does not prove coverage of Wi‑Fi 7’s full 16 spatial streams [6][14][19].

cited_passages.text: Rohde & Schwarz R&S®FSPN Phase Noise Analyzer and VCO Tester
Rohde & Schwarz R&S®FSWP Phase Noise Analyzer and VCO Tester

In the production phase of WLAN devices, all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time. Rohde & Schwarz has optimized the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester for this purpose. The instrument supports many cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi-Fi 6E, Wi-Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz in frequency with bandwidths up to 500 MHz. Leveraging the wide bandwidth, the R&S CMP180 will demonstrate at MWC its ability to verify a WLAN waveform with 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, a potential waveform candidate for the yet-to-be-defined Wi-Fi 8 (IEEE 802.11bn) standard. This feature shows that the cost-effective instrument is future-proof for users not only in production, but also in R&D.
